html:
A group of Greek philosophers of the 5th century BCE centred on Elea, a Greek colony in southern Italy. Its main figures were Parmenides and his pupil Zeno.

Parmenides argued in a poem that what is cannot come from nothing or pass into nothing. So, he concluded, true reality is one, unchanging and without motion, and the world of change our senses show is an illusion. Zeno defended him with paradoxes: swift Achilles can never catch a tortoise, and a flying arrow is at rest at every moment. These puzzles about infinity and motion are still discussed.

The Eleatics forced later thinkers to explain how change is possible without things coming from nothing. Empedocles answered with four unchanging elements, and Democritus with unchanging atoms moving in empty space. Plato wrote a dialogue named after Parmenides. Their style of strict argument, following reason even against the senses, was a turning point for Greek philosophy, opposed to the constant flux of Heraclitus.
sum: A group of Greek philosophers of the 5th century BCE centred on Elea, a Greek colony in southern Italy. Its main figures were Parmenides and his pupil Zeno.
